questions: Did these movements begin suddenly within the past few days?
Are you fully aware and able to respond normally while the movements occur?
Do the movements stop completely when you are asleep?
Can you briefly suppress the movements if you try?
Do you feel an uncomfortable urge or inner restlessness before moving?
Have you had any episodes of staring, loss of awareness, or inability to respond?
Have you bitten your tongue, lost bladder control, or been confused after an episode?
Did the movements start after a new medication was begun or a dose was increased?
Have you received metoclopramide, prochlorperazine, promethazine, or an antipsychotic medication recently?
Have you received opioids, gabapentin, pregabalin, valproate, lithium, cefepime, or another sedating medication recently?
Have you recently stopped or sharply reduced alcohol, benzodiazepines, or another regularly used drug?
Have you recently used cocaine, amphetamines, or another stimulant?
Have you had kidney, liver, thyroid, or blood-sugar problems?
Have you had vomiting, diarrhea, poor food or fluid intake, or prolonged fasting recently?
Have you had fever, severe headache, neck stiffness, or a recent infection?
Have you noticed confusion, unusual sleepiness, or personality changes?
Do the movements worsen when you hold your arms out or try to maintain a posture?
Do you have weakness, numbness, trouble speaking, trouble seeing, or difficulty walking?
Have you ever had similar movements before this illness?
Does anyone in your family have similar involuntary movements or a diagnosed movement disorder?

dx_raw:
DIAGNOSIS: Acquired hepatocerebral degeneration (hepatic parkinsonism/tremor) due to chronic hepatic dysfunction or portosystemic shunting with manganese deposition in the basal ganglia, accompanied by hyperammonemic hepatic encephalopathy

Alternative: Chronic liver disease–related hyperammonemic encephalopathy with tremor/myoclonus

Alternative: Acquired manganese neurotoxicity from hepatic manganese accumulation

Alternative: Wilson disease (unlikely given normal copper, ceruloplasmin, and urinary copper)
